## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

136: export function buildSpec(car, upgrades = {}) {
137:   const u = {
138:     engine: upgrades.engine | 0,
139:     tires: upgrades.tires | 0,
140:     weight: upgrades.weight | 0,
141:     gearbox: upgrades.gearbox | 0,
142:   };
143:   return {
144:     id: car.id,
145:     name: car.name,
146:     mass: car.mass * (1 - 0.03 * u.weight),
147:     torque: car.torque * (1 + 0.07 * u.engine),
148:     peakRpm: car.peakRpm,
149:     redline: car.redline,
150:     idle: car.idle,
151:     gears: car.gears.slice(),
152:     finalDrive: car.finalDrive * (1 + 0.02 * u.gearbox),
153:     wheelRadius: car.wheelRadius,
154:     cdA: car.cdA,
155:     grip: car.grip * (1 + 0.05 * u.tires),
156:     launchRpm: car.launchRpm,
157:   };
158: }

160: // Pequeno "dyno" pra exibir potência estimada no menu.
161: export function estimatePower(car, upgrades) {
162:   const s = buildSpec(car, upgrades);
163:   const rpm = s.peakRpm;
164:   const w = (rpm * Math.PI * 2) / 60;
165:   return Math.round((s.torque * w) / 745.7);

We need to figure out remaining issues. There are obvious bugs:

1. carModel `paintMaterial` makes new material per car; setPaint updates per model. Fine.
2. Brake light loop checks emissive.r > 0.5 and emissive.g < 0.2 - taillight material is shared mats.taillight across all cars, so player traversal toggles shared material (comment acknowledges). Fine.
3. In updateRace, when foul, greenReached eventually true via updateTree->onGreen. Then race still proceeds; finishRace sets win false. Fine.
4. Major bug: `positionForShowroom` calls `this.effects.clear()` before `effects` created? initTrack creates effects before openMenu. Fine.
5. `nextRival` uses careerWins. If careerWins >= RIVALS length, idx capped to last, extraCycles grows. Good.
6. `startRace` sets `this.playerModel.setPaint(...)` using paint id. Fine.
7. Physics: in `step`, during locked with throttle and clutch, engine rpm ramps to redline. launchRpm ~3900. When releasing, releaseRpm etc. Starting with clutch true and throttle, okay.
8. But after green, if player doesn't release clutch, engine still free; they must release. Fine.
9. Tach maybe huge.
10. UI scoreboard etc.

Need to run and inspect. Need npm install. Also test with playwright. Let's install first.

Below you will find a complete list of every known and reported Minecraft RTX issue, as well as their current status on Mojang's issue reporting site, [Mojira](https://bugs.mojang.com/).

The issues are listed based on priority, if an issue you've encountered is missing from this list, and you believe it is related to the game, report it through Mojira, but if you think it is related to Vanilla RTX, or Vanilla RTX App, report it to Cubeir 

If a reported or known Minecraft RTX issue is missing from this list in particular, a bug is miscategorized, has the wrong link, etc... please [open an issue](https://github.com/vanilla-rtx/Minecraft-RTX-Bug-Tracking/issues) or [a pull request](https://github.com/vanilla-rtx/Minecraft-RTX-Bug-Tracking/pulls).

## Table of Contents

- [🟥 Unresolved Issues](#-unresolved)
- [🟧 Issues Mojang Won't Fix](#-mojang-wont-fix)
- [🟨 Issues worked around by Supervanilla RTX, Vanilla RTX or other means](#-worked-around)
  - [Fixed by Supervanilla RTX](#fixed-by-supervanilla-rtx)
  - [Fixed by Vanilla RTX](#fixed-by-vanilla-rtx)
  - [Worked around by the Vanilla RTX App](#worked-around-by-the-vanilla-rtx-app)
- [🟩 Resolved Issues](#-resolved)
- [⚒️ Vanilla RTX Bug Tracking](#vanilla-rtx-bug-tracking)

## 🟥 Unresolved

These issues have been reported on Mojira, regardless of confirmation status, they remain unresolved. (Sorted based on severity, from highest to lowest).  
You will need to login or create an account to be able to vote.

- [MCPE-183773](https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MCPE/issues/MCPE-183773) - Entity UV Animations do not work once RTX is enabled.
- [MCPE-241723](https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MCPE/issues/MCPE-241723) - Animated flipbook textures no longer animate smoothly with ray tracing enabled

- [MCPE-119895](https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MCPE/issues/MCPE-119895) - Glass loses transparency at a distance with Ray Tracing on
- [MCPE-119941](https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MCPE/issues/MCPE-119941) - Transparent parts of an entity's texture stop particles from rendering behind them
- [MCPE-111406](https://bugs.mojang.com/browse/MCPE/issues/MCPE-111406) - Chests are culled when off screen with Ray Tracing on

index 2d1cee4..bb64679 100755
--- a/capture.sh
+++ b/capture.sh
@@ -1,4 +1,74 @@
 #!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Capture desktop and mobile evidence of the running preview.
+# Opens its own browser, writes final-desktop.png and final-mobile.png into
+# CAPTURE_DIR, closes the browser and leaves the app running.
+# Exit 75 = temporary navigation/browser infrastructure failure.
+# Exit 1  = script or rendering defect.
 set -euo pipefail
-cd "$(dirname "$0")"
-/usr/bin/time -p node "${RUNTIME_DIR:?}/scripts/default-capture.mjs"
+
+timed() { /usr/bin/time -p "$@"; }
+
+PROJECT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+cd "$PROJECT_DIR"
+
+if [[ -z "${CAPTURE_URL:-}" || -z "${CAPTURE_DIR:-}" ]]; then
+  echo "capture.sh requires CAPTURE_URL and CAPTURE_DIR." >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+if [[ ! "$CAPTURE_URL" =~ ^https?:// ]]; then
+  echo "CAPTURE_URL must be an http(s) URL (got '$CAPTURE_URL')." >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+if [[ -z "${RUNTIME_DIR:-}" || ! -f "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-capture.mjs" ]]; then
+  echo "RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-capture.mjs is missing; cannot drive Playwright." >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+# Evidence must stay outside the source tree.
+project_real="$(realpath -m "$PROJECT_DIR")"
+capture_real="$(realpath -m "$CAPTURE_DIR")"
+case "$capture_real/" in
+  "$project_real"/*)
+    echo "CAPTURE_DIR must be outside the project (got '$CAPTURE_DIR')." >&2
+    exit 1
+    ;;
+esac
+
+echo "==> Capturing $CAPTURE_URL into $CAPTURE_DIR"
+timed mkdir -p "$CAPTURE_DIR"
+
+# Keep only freshly captured evidence.
+for name in final-desktop.png final-mobile.png; do
+  if [[ -f "$CAPTURE_DIR/$name" ]]; then
+    timed rm -f "$CAPTURE_DIR/$name"
+  fi
+done
+
+# Wait for the game canvas instead of merely <body>, so a blank bootstrap page
+# is never accepted as rendered content.
+CAPTURE_READY_SELECTOR="${CAPTURE_READY_SELECTOR:-canvas}"
+export CAPTURE_READY_SELECTOR
+
+/usr/bin/time -p node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-capture.mjs"
+
+# Validate the evidence the controller will publish.
+for name in final-desktop.png final-mobile.png; do
+  file="$CAPTURE_DIR/$name"
+  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then
+    echo "Capture did not produce $name." >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  signature="$(head -c 8 "$file" | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')"
+  if [[ "$signature" != "89504e470d0a1a0a" ]]; then
+    echo "$name is not a PNG image." >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  size="$(stat -c %s "$file")"
+  if (( size <= 24 )); then
+    echo "$name is empty ($size bytes)." >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  echo "==> $name: $size bytes"
+done
+
+echo "==> Capture complete"

content.text:
PrismTextureStreamer

A Prism3D plugin that takes over cabin screens (GPS, dashboard, or any custom accessory) in Euro Truck Simulator 2 (or American Truck Simulator) and mirrors a live captured window onto them.

--- ## What it does Press **Ctrl+F8** in game to open an ImGui overlay. From there you can: - Add a **GPS** screen, **Dashboard** screen, or a **Custom** screen (The target `.tobj` MUST be a functional screen from a UI Script, such as `/ui/gps.sii`) - Pick a running application window as the source for that screen - Adjust target resolution and framerate - Apply changes Whatever's rendering in the picked window gets captured and blitted onto the truck's screen every frame. ## How it works ### 1. Redirecting the texture file A hook on Prism3D's `memserver_texture_queue_processor` walks the engine's pending texture object queue every tick. If a queued `tobj`'s path matches a screen's `original_texture` (e.g. `/vehicle/truck/share/gps.tobj`), the path is swapped for `override_texture` before the engine loads it. ### 2. Catching the texture at creation time The override `.tobj` still gets built into a real DirectX texture eventually, there's a hook on `ID3D11Device::CreateTexture2D`. Every creation call is checked against a fignerprint. The real game textures never match the fingerprint, so it's whats used to capture the screens texture. *This method is a bit "jank"... but it does work ;)* Once matched, the description is rewritten before the real `CreateTexture2D` is called: ```cpp D3D11_TEXTURE2D_DESC modifiedDesc = *pDesc; modifiedDesc.Format = DXGI_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM; modifiedDesc.Usage = D3D11_USAGE_DYNAMIC; modifiedDesc.CPUAccessFlags = D3D11_CPU_ACCESS_WRITE; modifiedDesc.MiscFlags = 0; modifiedDesc.Width = screen.targetLiveTextureWidth; modifiedDesc.Height = screen.targetLiveTextureHeight; ``` This gives us a CPU writable arbitrarily sized texture instead of the default game texture - then the resulting texture and its immediate context are cached on the `screen_t` for later. ### 3. Feeding it frames Every present call, each screen with a live texture and an active source: - Pulls the latest RGBA8 frame from its content source - `Map()`s the live texture with `D3D11_MAP_WRITE_DISCARD` - Copies row by row using nearest neighbor sampling if source and destination sizes differ, with an optional vertical flip - `Unmap()`s it ### 4. Forcing the screens to actually render The GPS/dashboard/custom screens are normally only drawn under specific in game conditions. `dllmain.cpp` patches the relevant conditional jump in the games process, flipping `JE` to `JMP` (and back) at runtime so the screen's render path is unconditionally taken whenever a screen of that type exists, and restored to normal when it doesn't. Addresses are found via pattern scanning, so it hopefully survives most game updates. ## Content sources Currently there's one source implementation, **`WindowSource`**, which finds a target window by executable name, then captures it every frame using `PrintWindow` + `GetDIBits` on a dedicated worker thread. The source uses a interface `IContentSource`, so other backends (a video file source, a mintor source, etc) can be implimented very easially in the future without touching the DX11 or menu code. ## Requirements - MinHook - Dear ImGui - SCS Telemetry SDK - DirectX 11 ## Known issues - Fingerprinting textures by dimensions/format means any other texture in the game that happens to match GPS/dashboard's size and format exactly would get caught too which is unlikely (if using unqiue dimentions), but not impossible. - Custom screens have no override_texture_size_w/h wiring in the menu yet, unlike GPS/Dashboard. ## Usage 1. Drop the compiled plugin DLL into your ETS2/ATS `plugins` folder (not a injected DLL) 2. Launch the game, Ctrl+F8 to open the menu 3. Add a screen, pick a source window, hit Apply ## Contributing PRs and issues are welcome, keep in mind: - If a pattern scan fails to resolve on a newer patch, that's the first thing to check before assuming something else is broken. (Same with any Prism3D structures inside `prism/prism.h`) - DO NOT use hard coded file offsets etc, keep with using pattern scans where possible. - If you're adding a new `IContentSource` (video file, monitor capture, etc.), implement it against the existing interface in `sources/content_source.h`. - Match existing code style so diffs stay reviewable and the project isnt a mess of multiple people. - Test on an actual ETS2 install before opening a PR. ---- ---- 67

## PRISM no jogo

**Novo `WindowFeed` em `src/three/liveScreens.js`**
- `getDisplayMedia` abre o seletor nativo de janela/aba/tela do navegador (equivalente ao seletor do plugin).

**Integração (`src/game.js`)**
- A captura assume o material da tela escolhida; telemetria e câmera de ré deixam de ser atualizadas enquanto estão ocultas (economia de GPU).
- Ao parar, tudo volta para telemetria/câmera; preferências de fps/enquadramento permanecem.

export function buildSpec(car, upgrades = {}) {
  const u = {
    engine: upgrades.engine | 0,
    tires: upgrades.tires | 0,
    weight: upgrades.weight | 0,
    gearbox: upgrades.gearbox | 0,
  };
  return {
    id: car.id,
    name: car.name,
    mass: car.mass * (1 - 0.03 * u.weight),
    torque: car.torque * (1 + 0.07 * u.engine),
    peakRpm: car.peakRpm,
    redline: car.redline,
    idle: car.idle,
    gears: car.gears.slice(),
    finalDrive: car.finalDrive * (1 + 0.02 * u.gearbox),
    wheelRadius: car.wheelRadius,
    cdA: car.cdA,
    grip: car.grip * (1 + 0.05 * u.tires),
    launchRpm: car.launchRpm,
  };
}

  const w = (rpm * Math.PI * 2) / 60;

}

This simplifies a lot and still delivers curve gameplay. The car's world position = point along spline + lateral offset; heading = spline tangent + lateral slip angle. Steering moves the car laterally, but corners require slowing because max lateral offset is limited by speed (grip). Player must brake before curves (HUD shows braking zone/line), otherwise the car slides to the outside and hits the wall, losing speed.

Now, a very important consideration: total effort. Let's focus on delivering:

1. Street circuit (~1.4 km, 5 curves), with walls, buildings, streetlights, start/finish gantries, start tree, and colored racing line.
2. Braking/acceleration line on the road + HUD coach ("FREIA 90m" / "ACELERA" / target speed).
3. Car follows the road, steers, drifts off line if too fast, crashes into barriers and loses speed.
4. Brake control on keyboard/mobile.
5. Gear display above the wheel (3D canvas).
6. Driver hands on wheel + right hand shifting (with shifter animation).
7. Add 5 "mod cars" entries, selectable in the garage, with style/accent differences and rival lineup updated.
8. Menu/HUD text updated for 1.4 km street race.
9. Keep Prism captures working.

Let's design the track numerically.

### Track design

Use segments with headings in degrees and lengths. Coordinate: x right, z forward. Heading 0 = +z. Turning right = positive heading change (clockwise in x-z plane? If heading angle measured from +z toward +x, then a right turn increases heading). Arc center for right turn: center = pos + normal_right * R, where normal_right = (cos(h), 0? in xz: (cos(h), ...)). For heading h (0=+z), direction = (sin h, cos h) in (x,z). Right normal = (cos h, -sin h). Arc around center: start angle from center to pos = ... Let's just simulate small steps with curvature: at each 1m step, heading += curvature * ds; pos += dir * ds. Curvature = 1/R (right positive). This is simple and robust, and transitions can be smoothed later.

Segments:
- straight 220m (launch + run-up) — start line at 0, tree at 12m.
- right 90° R=65 (length 102m)
- straight 140
- left 90° R=70 (110)
- straight 90
- right 45° R=80 (63)
- straight 70
- hairpin left 165° R=32 (92) — tight, requires braking
- straight 190
- chicane right 35 R=110 (67), straight 40, left 35 R=110 (67)
- straight 120
- left 75° R=85 (111)
- straight 160
- right 120° R=55 (115) — long sweeper
- straight 260 (finish straight)
Total ≈ 220+102+140+110+90+63+70+92+190+67+40+67+120+111+160+115+260 = 2017 m. That's long (2 km). Maybe too long for a 20s limit in updateRace (`raceClock - greenClock > 20` auto-end). Need to adjust to ~90s? Street race of 2km at avg 100 km/h → 72s. The current DNF timeout is 20s. Must change to track length / 15 m/s + margin. Rival AI target and race pacing.

User said "corrida maior que isso" (bigger than this) — good, 1.6–2.0 km. Let's target ~1.6 km, average ~120 km/h → ~50s. Increase timeout to 90s.

But note fuel/heat etc. no. Audio engine loop fine.

Let's verify self-intersection with a Python sim. Also compute curvature profile and target speeds for a 1.4g car: hairpin R=32 → vmax = sqrt(1.4*9.81*32) ≈ 21 m/s = 76 km/h. Braking from 200 km/h (55.5 m/s) at 1.0g: distance = v²/(2*9.81) ≈ 157m. So need long braking zones before hairpins — good gameplay.

Hairpin radius 32 might be too tight for the car; road half width 9.5; okay.

Let's generate and check. Also min distance between non-adjacent path points > 40m so roads don't overlap.

Then build the track from sampled points rather than analytic segments: 
- Sample every 2m with positions and headings from the integrated path.
- Compute curvature from heading change / ds, then smooth with a moving average window (e.g., ±8 samples = 16m) to make grip transitions and steering nice.
- Compute max speed profile using smoothed curvature and grip 1.35 (for best car) / 1.1.
- Ideal line offset from curvature: inside = sign(curv) * (halfWidth - 3.0) but smooth; use a low-pass of curvature sign; clamp; at hairpin, inside line 5.5m.
- Racing line ribbon mesh at that offset with color by target speed.
- Start/finish line positions.
- Build road mesh (tri strip) with UVs; sidewalks/curbs as tri strips; barrier walls; street props placed at intervals with normals; buildings placed at offset ~25-45m randomly; lights every 50m alternating sides; some billboards; tire stacks near corners (outside of apex).

Performance: Road 2000m/2m = 1000 segments; props maybe 150; buildings 60; lights 80. Fine.

```js
export function buildTrack() {
  const path = buildPath(); // {samples, length, halfWidth}
  ...
  return { group, setTree, update, LANE, FINISH: length, length, halfWidth, treePosition, sample, targetSpeedAt, idealOffsetAt, cornerInfo(distance), preview: ... };
}
```
Sampling:
```js
function sampleAt(d) {
  d = clamp(d, 0, length)
  const f = d / step; i0 = floor, i1...
  pos lerp, heading lerp (careful wrap), curvature lerp, normal...
}
```
Use object pooling? Return plain object each call — called ~3-5 times per frame, fine.

- `worldAt(distance, lateral, out)` returns x,z. `lateral` positive = right of travel. Position = point + normal*lateral.
- `headingAt(d)`.

Target speed:
- `speedLimit[i] = min(TOP, sqrt(GRIP*G / max(|curv|, 0.0005)))`.
- backward pass: for i from n-2 to 0: v[i] = min(v[i], sqrt(v[i+1]^2 + 2*BRAKE_DS)); where BRAKE_DS = 0.85*GRIP*G.
- forward pass? For acceleration out of corners: v[i+1] = min(v[i+1], sqrt(v[i]^2 + 2*ACCEL_DS)) with ACCEL_DS = 0.55*G (~5.4 m/s²). This makes exit speeds realistic. Then color green where v is limited by acceleration, red where braking.

- For color: compute per-sample "action": compare next target speed to current: if v[i+1] < v[i] - 0.5 → braking (red); if v[i+1] > v[i] + 0.5 → acceleration (green); else yellow. Hmm at 2m sampling, speed differences are tiny. Use lookahead 10m: action = sign(v[i+10]-v[i]); color red if v[i] < 0.85*maxLocal? Let's use a simpler visual scheme:
  - Braking zones: sample is red if v[i] < 0.75 * vmaxStraight AND v[i-20] < v[i+20]?? 
  Better: color by target speed ratio to top speed: red < 0.5, orange < 0.7, yellow < 0.85, green >= 0.85. This produces red near hairpins, yellow mid-corner, green exits/straights. Meets "linha de freio e aceleração na curva" as a colored line.
  Additionally, HUD tells "FREIA" or "ACELERA" based on action.

- Ideal line: offset = sign(curvature) * min(5.5, |curv|*R?) Actually max offset ~ (halfWidth-2.2) * tanh(|curv|*80). For curv=1/32=0.031 → tanh(2.5)=0.987 → ~6.3m. For 1/65=0.015 → tanh(1.2)=0.83 → 5.3m. For 1/110=0.009 → 0.58 → 3.7m. Good, but the line should be smooth; use smoothing of curvature before.

- Brake markers: add "100", "50" boards before heavy corners at the side. Also brake distance signs.

- For each sample (every 3m), point at ideal offset, width 0.5m. Two vertices per sample (offset ±0.3), y=0.035. Colors per sample. Use vertexColors, MeshBasicMaterial({vertexColors:true, transparent:true, opacity:0.8, depthWrite:false, polygonOffset...}). Maybe render as dashed: alpha? Vertex colors only RGB; no alpha. Could alternate gaps by skipping segments every few meters to make it look like a guide line? A continuous ribbon with color is clearer. Add slight emissive glow with additive? Basic material is unlit and bright; with toneMapped false to pop. Use `MeshBasicMaterial({ vertexColors: true, toneMapped: false })`, opacity 0.9.
- A second thinner centerline? Keep one.

HUD coach:
- `track.advice(distance, speed)` returns {action:"brake"|"accelerate"|"hold", distanceToCurve, targetSpeed, curveDir, severity}. Compute nearest braking zone ahead: find first sample where target speed < current speed - 2, distance to it. Or simpler: compare current speed to targetSpeed at lookahead d+20m? For a proper "FREIA 120m" we need the upcoming corner's entry speed. Use the precomputed profile: `needBrake = vTarget[d] - speed`; if vTarget[d] < speed - 1.5 → brake now; distance until the profile rises? Also show upcoming: find the minimum vTarget in the next 250m and the distance where braking must start: the largest d' > d such that sqrt(vTarget[d']² + 2*b*dist) ... Actually vTarget[d] already accounts for upcoming braking via backward pass, so `vTarget[d]` is the max speed you can carry now. If current speed > vTarget[d] + 1 → "FREIA". Distance to corner: find next index where |curv| > threshold (e.g., 1/120). Show "CURVA ESQ 120m". Direction from curvature.
- Also "ACELERA" if vTarget[d+30] > speed + 2 and no brake need.
- HUD bar: a horizontal gauge where marker shows current speed vs target; red when over.

Rival target times: implement `simulateTargetET(spec, track)`:

```js
const sim = new DragSim(spec);
... launch ...
while (dist < track.length && guard < 120*120) {
  const target = track.targetSpeedAt(dist + 5) * (0.94 + ...); // AI pace
  const brake = sim.speed > target ? clamp((sim.speed-target)/8,0,1) : 0;
  const throttle = brake > 0.1 ? 0 : (sim.wheelspin > 0.6 ? 0.6 : 1);
```

## Objective
- Improve the DRAG BRASIL car interior and integrate live external content into its cockpit screens, adapting the linked repository’s functionality for the browser game.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

- The linked repository’s PrismTextureStreamer is a C++/DirectX 11 plugin for ETS2/ATS and cannot run in the browser; implemented equivalent browser capture instead.
- No changes were made to physics.

- `npm run build` completes with the existing large-chunk advisory.

- (none)

- The browser cannot use the repository’s native DirectX hook or enumerate windows directly; capture relies on the browser’s native source selector and requires HTTPS or localhost plus a user gesture.

1. (none)

- `src/three/carModel.js`: Cockpit and interior model.
- `src/three/textures.js`: Procedural interior textures.
- `src/three/liveScreens.js`: `WindowFeed` and live screen textures.

Simpler, robust approach: track defined by a centerline spline sampled at fixed intervals (arc-length parameter). Functions: pointAt(s), tangentAt(s), curvatureAt(s). Player state: `distance` (arc length), `lateral` (offset from centerline, positive right). Existing sim has distance and lateral/lateralV; track currently uses `sim.lateral` for position x. Then the car's world transform: position = pointAt(d) + normal * lateral; heading = tangent angle + small steer yaw. The camera and rival use same.

Curvature handling: The path itself curves; the car follows it automatically (as if steering). The grip limit: max lateral accel = grip * g. Required lateral accel = v² * |kappa|. If required > available, the car understeers: lateral drift toward the outside (sign of curvature). Add drift: `lateralV += (v²*kappa - grip*g*sign(kappa)) * dt` when exceeding. ## Scope plan

### 1. Cars from the mod pack / "street" car pack
The mod repo contains Burnout Paradise car mods (binary .BIN, Windows game), can't import. But the user wants "esses carros". Best adaptation: add a themed car pack inspired by the pack's cars to the catalog, with new body types? That's costly. However, we can add 4 new cars using data only (same procedural body but different paint/stat), names from the pack (e.g. "IKUSA GT", "HOT ROD CIRCUIT", "STEEL WHEELS GT", "OVAL CHAMP"), with tags crediting the pack. But visually indistinguishable except paint might feel cheap. Perhaps add body style variants to createCarModel: `bodyStyle` param ("muscle", "hotrod", "sport", "gt") with small differences (wing, scoop, roof height, fender flares). Hmm, scope creep.

Given time constraints, I think a reasonable adaptation: add 4 "street pack" cars to CARS (total 8) with names inspired by the pack, each with `body` variants, and garage lists them. But that requires UI fits (garage list handles it via CARS). Save default only owns falcao. Prices moderate. Also RIVALS can use new cars for variety.

Yet the user's central asks are interior character, longer curvy track, brake/accel line, gear above wheel. The cars part is "coloca esse carros" — I should provide something concrete. I'll add 4 cars from the pack naming with distinct body kits via a `body` field and modify carModel to vary silhouette (wheel arch flares, hood scoop, wing style, roof). Keep it procedural and cheap.

Maybe I should also add a note in the README about the pack being a Burnout mod and that the game includes an adapted tribute pack.

Let me decide: add cars:
- `ikusa` — "IKUSA GT" (B'z Ikusa GT), sport GT, price 5200
- `hotrod` — "CIRCUIT HOT ROD" (Circuit City Hot Rod), price 9500, big torque
- `steel` — "STEEL WHEELS GT" (Steel Wheels GT), price 13000
- `oval` — "OVAL CHAMP" (Bestbuy Oval Champ), price 1900
Maybe 3 to keep garage manageable. I'll add 4.

Body variants:
- `hotrod`: exposed blower/scoop, no rear wing maybe, taller rear tires? Simple: add big hood scoop, side exhaust, smaller roof.
- `gt`: wide fenders, big wing.
- `oval`: stripes, no wing, chrome bumpers.
- default muscle: current.

I can implement cosmetic variants with parameters: `body: { scoop, wing, wide, stripe, roof }`. Keep it simple: variant affects wing style and scoop/wide fenders only via `kit` string in createCarModel options. Pass car.kit in rebuildPlayerCar and rival creation.

### 2. Realistic interior with driver, hands on wheel, shifting
Add to carModel.js (interior block):
- Driver group seated at x=-0.37, z=-0.42.
- Torso: racing suit (dark navy/red), chest, shoulders, neck, head with helmet (open visor / full-face) — head at ~1.31, tilted slightly forward.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Capture desktop and mobile evidence of the running preview.
# Opens its own browser, writes final-desktop.png and final-mobile.png into
# CAPTURE_DIR, closes the browser and leaves the app running.
# Exit 75 = temporary navigation/browser infrastructure failure.
# Exit 1  = script or rendering defect.
set -euo pipefail

timed() { /usr/bin/time -p "$@"; }

PROJECT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
cd "$PROJECT_DIR"

if [[ -z "${CAPTURE_URL:-}" || -z "${CAPTURE_DIR:-}" ]]; then
  echo "capture.sh requires CAPTURE_URL and CAPTURE_DIR." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [[ ! "$CAPTURE_URL" =~ ^https?:// ]]; then
  echo "CAPTURE_URL must be an http(s) URL (got '$CAPTURE_URL')." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [[ -z "${RUNTIME_DIR:-}" || ! -f "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-capture.mjs" ]]; then
  echo "RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-capture.mjs is missing; cannot drive Playwright." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Evidence must stay outside the source tree.
project_real="$(realpath -m "$PROJECT_DIR")"
capture_real="$(realpath -m "$CAPTURE_DIR")"
case "$capture_real/" in
  "$project_real"/*)
    echo "CAPTURE_DIR must be outside the project (got '$CAPTURE_DIR')." >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

echo "==> Capturing $CAPTURE_URL into $CAPTURE_DIR"
timed mkdir -p "$CAPTURE_DIR"

# Keep only freshly captured evidence.

## Objective
- Improve DRAG BRASIL with cars inspired by the linked mod collection, a realistic cockpit showing the driver’s hands on the wheel and shifting, and a longer street-racing course with curves that require braking and acceleration.
- Move the gear display above the steering wheel.

## Requirements
- User asked: “coloca esse carros mas quero a interna realista mostrando o personagem com a mão no volante e trocando macha e quero a corrida maior que isso ,vai ser uma arrancada de rua então a pista vai ser longa e com várias curvar onde tem que desacelerar para não bater mas quero uma linha de freio e aceleração na curva e as marchar tem que ficar em cima do volante”.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- The linked repository is for Burnout Paradise Remastered; its Windows mod installer and game-specific car assets are not directly usable in this browser Three.js game.
- Earlier work implemented browser-based live screen capture as an equivalent to the linked ETS2/ATS DirectX plugin; physics was not changed during that work.

## Work State
### Completed
- Earlier cockpit and interior overhaul, camera framing updates, and live screen capture for cockpit screens with PRISM controls.
- Earlier checks covered boot, menu, race, finish, and a synthetic live video feed; reported zero console errors. `npm run build` completed with an existing large-chunk advisory.

### Active
- Investigating how to adapt the new car, cockpit-driver, gear-display, and curved-course requests to the existing procedural game.
- Inspected `mod-cars-releases`; its release pack contains Burnout-specific files and does not provide drop-in browser-ready models.

### Blocked
- The linked repository does not provide directly usable browser assets or an implementation compatible with this game; suitable cars must be recreated or sourced in a browser-compatible format.

## Next Move
1. Implement or adapt car visuals and animate a visible driver’s hands to grip the steering wheel and shift.
2. Relocate the gear indicator above the wheel.
3. Extend the course into a longer curved street race, adding curve-aware braking/acceleration guidance and collision handling as appropriate.
4. Build and visually verify the changes.

## Relevant Files
- `src/three/carModel.js`: Procedural car, cockpit, steering wheel, seats, and interior.
- `src/three/track.js`: Current track geometry and roadside elements.

- `src/physics.js`: Current vehicle simulation.
- `index.html`: HUD and gear display markup.
- `src/style.css`: HUD and control styling.

import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { readFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
process.env.DISPLAY ||= ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim()
const cfg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
const out = '/tmp/opencode/shots2'
mkdirSync(out, { recursive: true })

const browser = await chromium.launch(cfg.browser.launchOptions)
const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1280, height: 720 }, deviceScaleFactor: 1 })
const errors = []
page.on('console', (m) => { if (m.type() === 'error') errors.push(m.text()) })
page.on('pageerror', (e) => errors.push('pageerror: ' + e.message))
await page.goto('http://localhost:3000/', { waitUntil: 'networkidle' })
await page.bringToFront()
await page.waitForTimeout(600)
await page.screenshot({ path: join(out, '00-boot.jpg'), type: 'jpeg', quality: 72 })
if (await page.locator('#btn-boot').isVisible()) await page.click('#btn-boot')
await page.waitForTimeout(900)
await page.screenshot({ path: join(out, '01-menu.jpg'), type: 'jpeg', quality: 72 })
await page.click('#btn-race')
await page.waitForTimeout(1500)

const put = async (distance, speed, gear, opts = {}) => page.evaluate(({ distance, speed, gear, opts }) => {
  const g = window.__dragBrasil
  g.greenReached = true
  g.greenClock = 0
  g.raceClock = 10 + distance / 40
  g.phase = 'racing'
  g.playerRunStart = 0
  g.foul = false
  g.cameraMode = opts.camera || 'cockpit'
  g.steer = opts.steer || 0
  g.steerTarget = opts.steer || 0
  const s = g.playerSim
  s.distance = distance
  s.speed = speed
  s.gear = gear
  s.engineRpm = g.playerSpec.idle + (g.playerSpec.redline - g.playerSpec.idle) * (opts.rpm ?? 0.7)
  s.clutch = false
  s.prevClutch = false
  s.shiftTimer = 0
  if (opts.shift) { g.playerModel.driver.shift(); g.playerModel.driver.update(0.19, { steer: opts.steer || 0, time: 1 }) }
  g._gearShown = 0
  g.updateCarVisuals(0.016)
  g.updateHud()
  g.renderer.render(g.scene, g.camera)
}, { distance, speed, gear, opts })

// cockpit na reta antes da curva 1
await put(240, 78, 4, { rpm: 0.82, steer: 0.22 })
await page.waitForTimeout(900)
await page.screenshot({ path: join(out, '02-cockpit.jpg'), type: 'jpeg', quality: 74 })

// cockpit no meio da troca de marcha (mão na alavanca)
await put(430, 46, 3, { rpm: 0.9, shift: true, steer: -0.3 })
await page.waitForTimeout(700)
await page.screenshot({ path: join(out, '03-shift.jpg'), type: 'jpeg', quality: 74 })

// cockpit dentro da curva 2
await put(700, 38, 3, { rpm: 0.74, steer: 0.5 })
await page.waitForTimeout(700)
await page.screenshot({ path: join(out, '04-curve.jpg'), type: 'jpeg', quality: 74 })

// câmera externa mostrando carro e piloto
await put(900, 52, 4, { rpm: 0.8, camera: 'chase', steer: -0.18 })
await page.waitForTimeout(900)
await page.screenshot({ path: join(out, '05-chase.jpg'), type: 'jpeg', quality: 74 })

const info = await page.evaluate(() => {
  const g = window.__dragBrasil
  return {
    mode: g.mode, finish: Math.round(g.finishDistance), corners: g.track.corners.length,
    startS: Math.round(g.startS), finishS: Math.round(g.track.FINISH_S),
    total: Math.round(g.track.LENGTH), gear: g.playerSim.gear,
    hudGear: document.getElementById('hud-gear')?.textContent,
    advice: document.getElementById('rl-advice')?.textContent,
    corner: document.getElementById('rl-corner')?.textContent,
    target: document.getElementById('rl-target')?.textContent,
  }
})
console.log(JSON.stringify({ info, errors }, null, 2))
await browser.close()

## Objective
- Expand DRAG BRASIL from a quarter-mile drag race into a longer street race with curves, braking guidance, and collisions.
- Add inspired car options and a realistic cockpit driver with animated hands and shifting; place the gear display above the steering wheel.

## Requirements
- Use reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- Visually verify changes and inspect only the latest screenshot, saved as a small JPEG at a viewport no wider than 1280px.

## Decisions
- The linked Burnout Paradise Remastered mod collection is not directly usable as browser-ready Three.js assets; adapt its car inspiration with procedural models.
- The course follows a spline and race distance is measured along the track; curve speed guidance, braking/acceleration line, and wall impacts are being integrated.

## Work State
### Completed
- Replaced the straight track with a procedural curved course, including road geometry, walls, racing-line colors, braking signs, and start/finish structures.
- Added extra procedural car catalog entries and body kits inspired by the collection.
- Added a procedural cockpit driver, articulated arms, shifting animation, and in-car gear display above the steering wheel.
- Updated HUD and help text for the street-course format, braking, remaining distance, and racing-line guidance.

### Active
- Integrate course distance and curvature into the race simulation, rival behavior, vehicle placement, cameras, and HUD; verify these changes build and run correctly.
- Check/resolve likely integration defects in the latest edits, including track API compatibility, game-state references, UI updates, and car-model return fields.

### Blocked
- No suitable browser-ready assets from the linked mod collection; cars are being recreated procedurally instead.

## Next Move
1. Run `npm run build` and fix syntax/runtime or API mismatches.
2. Inspect relevant game, physics, and model APIs; validate the track’s start, finish, and race-distance mapping.
3. Visually test menu, cockpit race, curves/braking line, collision behavior, and finish using the latest screenshot at ≤1280px; save it as JPEG.
4. Report assumptions and verification results; preserve existing uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `src/three/track.js`: New spline course, racing line, corner profile, and track API.
- `src/game.js`: Race flow, positioning, rival logic, driver visuals, and course HUD integration.
- `src/physics.js`: Steering, corner grip, and wall collision behavior.
- `src/three/carModel.js`: Procedural car kits, cockpit driver, animated arms, and gear display.
- `src/data.js`: Car catalog and rival assignments.
- `index.html`: Updated HUD, controls, and help content.
- `src/style.css`: Racing-line HUD and gear-display styling.
- `src/ui.js`: Dynamic race-line and course distance updates.
- `dist/index.html`: Previously modified build output.

## Important Context
- Latest edits are uncommitted; earlier `git status` showed `dist/index.html` modified, and additional source changes have since been made.
- The latest history ends after raising the player lateral limit to `3.9`; no build or visual verification has yet been reported.
- `src/ui.js` still has some quarter-mile fallback values; `src/three/liveScreens.js` defaults finish distance to `402.336`.

import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { readFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
process.env.DISPLAY ||= ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim()
const cfg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
const out = '/tmp/opencode/shots3'
mkdirSync(out, { recursive: true })

const browser = await chromium.launch(cfg.browser.launchOptions)
const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1280, height: 720 }, deviceScaleFactor: 1 })
await page.goto('http://localhost:3000/', { waitUntil: 'networkidle' })
await page.waitForTimeout(500)
await page.click('#btn-boot')
await page.waitForTimeout(600)
await page.click('#btn-race')
await page.waitForTimeout(1100)

const data = await page.evaluate(() => {
  const g = window.__dragBrasil
  const THREE = window.__THREE
  g.update = function () {}
  g.playerSim.distance = 240
  g.playerSim.speed = 78
  g.playerSim.gear = 4
  g.playerSim.engineRpm = g.playerSpec.redline * 0.82
  g.greenReached = true
  g.phase = 'racing'
  g.playerRunStart = 0
  g.cameraMode = 'cockpit'
  g.updateCarVisuals(0.016)
  g.updateCamera(0.6)
  g.updateCamera(0.6)
  g.renderer.render(g.scene, g.camera)

  const rc = new THREE.Raycaster()
  const out = []
  for (const [x, y] of [[0, -0.35], [0, -0.55], [0, -0.75], [0.1, -0.65], [-0.1, -0.6], [0.2, 0.0], [-0.2, 0.0]]) {

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand DRAG BRASIL into a long street drag race with multiple curves, braking/acceleration guidance, and collisions.
- Add cars inspired by `https://github.com/TopGunMaster-source/mod-cars-releases.git` and improve the cockpit with a visible driver, animated hands/shifting, and a gear display above the steering wheel.

## Requirements
- Keep the race a street-style launch, but make the course longer with several curves that require slowing down to avoid crashes.
- Show a brake/acceleration line through curves and keep the gear display above the steering wheel.
- Use reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finished.
- Visually verify changes and inspect only the latest screenshot, saved as a small JPEG at a viewport no wider than 1280px.

## Decisions
- The track uses a spline, with race distance measured along its length; curve speed guidance, racing-line colors, and wall impacts are integrated or being validated.
- Procedural car models are being used because mod collection assets were not directly usable as browser-ready Three.js assets; the latest repository URL still needs checking for usable assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Replaced the straight course with a procedural curved track; the current course is about 2.46 km total, with a race distance of about 2.23 km and 15 detected corners.
- Added procedural car catalog entries/body kits, a cockpit driver with animated arms and shifting, and an in-car gear display above the steering wheel.
- Updated the HUD/help for course distance, braking, and racing-line guidance.
- `npm run build` succeeds; browser run reported no console/page errors during the scripted capture.

### Active
- Improve and visually verify the cockpit view: recent changes adjust camera placement/FOV, driver visibility, cabin lighting, and wheel/hand appearance, but final visual quality remains unresolved.
- Validate a real race through countdown, acceleration, shifting, curves, collisions, and finish; earlier browser testing was inconclusive because the car remained in staging.
- Check whether assets in the user’s latest mod repository can be used or must remain procedural.

### Blocked
- No confirmed browser-ready assets have been identified from the mod collection; direct compatibility of the latest URL has not been investigated.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the latest cockpit screenshot at `/tmp/opencode/shots3/annotated.png` or capture a new one after current edits; save the final reviewed image as a small JPEG at ≤1280px.
2. Run `npm run build`, then validate a complete playable race and fix any simulation, HUD, collision, or finish issues.
3. Investigate the latest mod repository for usable assets; otherwise continue with procedural adaptations.
4. Summarize assumptions and verification results when finished.

## Relevant Files
- `src/three/track.js`: Spline course, corner profile, racing line, and track API.
- `src/game.js`: Race flow, positioning, cameras, driver visuals, and course HUD integration.
- `src/physics.js`: Steering, corner grip, and wall collision behavior.
- `src/three/carModel.js`: Procedural car kits, cockpit driver, articulated arms, and gear display.
- `src/data.js`: Car catalog and rival assignments.
- `src/ui.js`: Race-line and course-distance HUD updates.
- `src/style.css`: HUD and cockpit-related styling.
- `index.html`: HUD and controls/help copy.
- `dist/index.html`: Previously modified build output.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; preserve them.
- Latest build passed with a Vite warning about a JavaScript chunk exceeding 500 kB.
- A scripted browser run had no reported errors, but it did not confirm active driving because the race remained in staging.
- `/tmp/opencode/shots3/annotated.png` is a diagnostic screenshot, not yet confirmed as the requested final JPEG.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand DRAG BRASIL into a street-style racing mod with a longer, curvy course and race-driving mechanics.
- Adapt cars inspired by `https://github.com/TopGunMaster-source/mod-cars-releases.git`, add curve braking guidance, realistic steering, and a gear display/shifter above the steering wheel.

## Requirements
- Keep the street-style launch; add multiple curves where slowing down matters.
- Show a racing line and cues for when to brake through curves.
- Make steering feel like actual driving; place the gear display/shifter above the steering wheel.
- Make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and briefly note them when finished.
- Visually verify changes using the latest screenshot, a small JPEG, at a viewport no wider than 1280px.

## Decisions
- Use a spline track, measure race distance along it, and integrate curve-speed guidance, racing-line colors, and wall impacts.
- Use procedural car models because browser-ready assets have not been confirmed in the Burnout Paradise Remastered mod repository.

## Work State

- Replaced the straight course with a procedural curved track of about 2.46 km, with a race distance of about 2.23 km and 15 detected corners.

# Skill: opencode-zen-completions

# OpenCode Zen completions

Use this skill when an implementation needs to send a prompt to the OpenCode Zen completions API. Keep the API call separate from product code unless the user explicitly asks to integrate it.

## Endpoints

- Models: `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/models`
- Completions: `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions`

The API is OpenAI-compatible. For the public OpenCode CLI-compatible request, use `Authorization: Bearer public`, `Content-Type: application/json`, and the client headers shown below. Treat model availability as live data: query the models endpoint before selecting a model when the exact model matters.

## Model selection

```sh
curl -sS https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/models \
  | jq -r '.data[].id | select(endswith("-free"))'
```

Prefer a currently listed `*-free` model when the user requests free usage. Known examples include `deepseek-v4-flash-free`, `muse-spark-1.2-contributor-free`, `mimo-v2.5-free`, `hy3-free`, `ling-3.0-flash-fin-free`, `nemotron-3-ultra-free`, `nemotron-3.5-lightning-free`, and `laguna-s-2.1-free`, but this list can change.

## Completion request

```sh
curl -sS https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer public' \
  -H 'User-Agent: opencode/1.15.9 ai-sdk/provider-utils/4.0.23 runtime/bun/1.3.14' \
  -H 'X-Opencode-Client: cli' \
  -H 'X-Opencode-Project: global' \
  -d '{"model":"mimo-v2.5-free","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<implementation prompt>"}],"stream":false}' \
  | jq
```

Use `stream: true` only when incremental output is useful. Check the HTTP status and API error object before consuming the completion. Non-streaming text is commonly at `.choices[0].message.content`; inspect the returned shape if the provider reports an error or a different format.

## Operating rules

- Never put private API keys, credentials, or sensitive source material into prompts or committed scripts.
- Treat completions as implementation assistance: review them against the repository, tests, security requirements, and exact scope. Generated text is not proof that code works.
- For application integrations, keep the endpoint and model configurable through environment variables or existing project configuration.
- On model/availability errors, refresh the model list. Do not silently substitute a paid or unrelated model when free usage was requested.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand DRAG BRASIL into a street-style racing mod with a longer, curvy course and race-driving mechanics.
- Adapt cars inspired by `https://github.com/TopGunMaster-source/mod-cars-releases.git`, add curve-braking guidance, realistic steering, and a gear display/shifter above the steering wheel.

## Requirements
- Keep the street-style launch; add multiple curves where slowing down matters.
- Show a racing line and cues for when to brake through curves.
- Make steering feel like actual driving; place the gear display/shifter above the steering wheel.
- Make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and briefly note them when finished.
- Visually verify changes using a fresh screenshot, a small JPEG, at a viewport no wider than 1280px.

## Decisions
- Use a spline track, measure race distance along it, and integrate curve-speed guidance, racing-line colors, and wall impacts.
- Use procedural car models because browser-ready assets have not been confirmed in the Burnout Paradise Remastered mod repository.

## Work State
### Completed
- Replaced the straight course with a procedural curved track about 2.46 km long, with a race distance of about 2.23 km and 15 detected corners.
- Added procedural car catalog entries/body kits, an animated cockpit driver, articulated arms/shifting, and an in-car gear display above the steering wheel.
- Updated HUD/help for course distance, braking, and racing-line guidance.
- `npm run build` succeeds; Vite warns that the JavaScript chunk exceeds 500 kB.
- A previous browser check reported no JavaScript errors; a 1280×720 cockpit JPEG was saved and inspected.
- Rebuilt after those changes; no new application code changes were made during the latest race-validation attempts.

### Active
- Validate a live keyboard-controlled race from staging through countdown, clutch release, acceleration, steering, curves, collisions, and finish.
- Capture and inspect a fresh JPEG at no more than 1280px wide.

### Blocked
- Latest Playwright attempts could not connect to `http://127.0.0.1:3002/` (`net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`); the background server command reported its serving URL but did not remain reachable during tests.

## Next Move
1. Restart the preview server in a persistent session and confirm it is reachable before opening Playwright.
2. Run the existing race test at `/tmp/opencode/live-race.mjs`; diagnose any launch/control issue and validate the race.
3. Save and inspect a fresh small JPEG at a viewport no wider than 1280px.
4. Summarize assumptions and verification results; preserve uncommitted changes, including generated `dist` output.

## Relevant Files
- `src/three/track.js`: spline course, corner profile, racing line, and track API.
- `src/game.js`: race flow, player controls, camera, driver visuals, and course HUD integration.
- `src/physics.js`: steering, corner grip, and wall collision behavior.
- `src/three/carModel.js`: procedural car kits, cockpit driver, articulated arms, and gear display.
- `src/data.js`: car catalog and rival assignments.
- `src/ui.js`: racing-line and course-distance HUD updates.
- `src/style.css`: HUD and cockpit styling.
- `index.html`: HUD and controls/help copy.
- `dist/index.html`: generated build output.
- `/tmp/opencode/live-race.mjs`: latest attempted live race test.
- `/tmp/opencode/final-review/latest-cockpit.jpg`: previous 1280×720 cockpit screenshot.
- `/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime/scripts/default-capture.mjs`: available capture flow, but its defaults use 1440px desktop and mobile sizes rather than the requested 1280px test.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; preserve the working tree and generated `dist` files.
- Previous live attempts remained in staging (`greenReached: false`) and did not verify launch or finish; no browser errors were reported then.
- The latest test script sequences boot, race start, clutch plus throttle, then steering/shifting/braking, but has not run successfully due to preview-server connection failures.
